title: dynamic-sli-weighting-and-query-budgeting-for-console-analytics
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: High-cardinality tenants and ad-hoc analytics queries are generating noisy SLI alerts and unpredictable query costs, causing alert fatigue for SREs and unexpected billing spikes for some customers. Goal: Implement a per-tenant dynamic SLI weighting mechanism + enforce query budgeting in the analytics ingest and query pipeline so alerts are meaningful and cost is bounded without degrading detection of real regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant SLI weight computed and stored in metadata service (hot path read path < 2ms)
Alerting system applies dynamic weight to SLI signals; top-10 noisy tenants no longer trigger >50% of low-priority alerts
Query budget enforcement prevents single-tenant query spikes from exceeding configured daily budget and returns 429 for over-budget queries
Dashboards show cost per-tenant per-query and SLI-weighted error rates; sample dashboards linked below
End-to-end benchmark: additional p50 latency for analytics query path < 10ms at 95th percentile after adding weight lookups
Runbook updated with mitigation steps and postmortem checklist
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed. Validated approach of computing weights from steady-state token throughput, error-rate volatility, and historical alert frequency. Prototype in python notebook: /drive/Shared/Analytics/sli-weighting-spike.ipynb
2026-03-05: Design doc posted for review: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/Dynamic+SLI+Weighting+and+Query+Budgeting. Feedback from PM & SRE requested by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-09: Design review notes: prefer asynchronous weight recomputation cadence (5m) to avoid hot metadata writes; SRE recommended 1% capped smoothing to avoid weight oscillation. Added opt-in per-customer overrides for enterprise customers.
2026-03-11: Prototype middleware implemented that reads weight from metadata cache (Redis) and applies weight to alert aggregation. Perf microbenchmarks: extra 3.5ms median, 9.8ms p95 on test infra.

2026-03-12: Initial query budget enforcement PoC merged to feature branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123. Uses token-cost estimator + per-tenant token counters with daily TTL. Returns structured error with budget_remaining and reset_ts.

2026-03-14: Stakeholder sync: PM accepted scope for MVP. SRE requested a circuit-breaker and emergency override endpoint for support. Added to follow-ups. Plan to run canary for 72h on non-critical tenants before broader rollout.
notes: Trade-offs: heavier weighting will mute signals from noisy tenants; to avoid missing real regressions we combine weight with volatility scoring and maintain a small fraction of unweighted signal for anomaly detection. Operational complexity: introduces per-tenant state and counters; mitigations include sharded counters, TTLs, and an emergency bypass. Next steps: implement circuit-breaker, canary rollout, SLO dashboard updates, and coordinate with Pricing for customer-facing budget notifications.
